summary: BUG-206 fix VERIFICATION FAILED. The added foodId reverse-lookup useEffect (RecipeBulkEditor.jsx L95-111) does NOT populate foodId on existing standard recipes. Root cause: React effect ordering — the reverse-lookup useEffect depends only on [foodsMaster]. When foodsMaster loads AFTER rows are hydrated by useEffect#1 (L74-78), the reverse-lookup runs but its enclosed `rows` closure may be stale OR when parent re-passes `recipes` prop, useEffect#1 re-hydrates rows (foodId=null) and reverse-lookup does NOT re-fire. Empirically: after mount, ALL 92/92 rows have foodId=null even though 92/92 names would match foodsMaster if the logic ran. The new client-side validation at L208 correctly surfaces this as '✗ Menu food link missing — cannot save' (better UX than the previous confusing 422), but the underlying enrichment does not execute — so V9 Batch Save still FAILS and RT-1 Persistence still FAILS. Regression tests PASS (Add Recipe food picker: 98 options; Card view toggle back: 92 cards).

action_items: PRIMARY FIX: The reverse-lookup useEffect at RecipeBulkEditor.jsx L97-111 fails to populate foodId. Recommended fix: MERGE the reverse-lookup INTO the row hydration useEffect#1 (L74-78) so both happen atomically when EITHER recipes or foodsMaster changes. Example: `useEffect(() => { const norm = (recipes||[]).map(normaliseRecipe); if (foodsMaster.length) { norm.forEach(r => { if (!r.isNew && !r.foodId) { const m = foodsMaster.find(f => (f.name||f.food_name||'').trim().toLowerCase() === (r.name||'').trim().toLowerCase()); if (m) r.foodId = String(m.id); } }); } setRows(norm); ... }, [recipes, recipeType, foodsMaster]);` — then remove the separate reverse-lookup useEffect entirely.

ALTERNATIVE (minimal-diff) FIX: Change useEffect#3 dependency array from `[foodsMaster]` to `[foodsMaster, rows.length]` OR to `[foodsMaster, recipes]`. This ensures the reverse-lookup re-runs whenever rows are re-hydrated by useEffect#1. Keep the existing changed-check to avoid infinite loops.

OPTIONAL BEST PRACTICE: Do the enrichment INSIDE normaliseRecipe by passing foodsMaster as an argument (functional style, no effect ordering concerns). Example: `normaliseRecipe(r, foodsMaster)` — enrich once at hydrate time.
After fix: retest V9 (save prep=55) and RT-1 (reload → verify prep=55) using recipe id 4874 (food_id 168408, name='50-50 Choco Lava'). Then revert prep back to 10 to leave preprod clean.
critical_code_review_comments: RecipeBulkEditor.jsx L97-111 (BUG-206 fix): The useEffect closure captures `rows` from the render where it was scheduled. However, the dep array is [foodsMaster] with eslint-disable, so it only re-runs when foodsMaster ref changes. Since useEffect#1 (L74-78) fires whenever `recipes` or `recipeType` change (which parent MAY re-trigger via prop reference changes), rows get re-hydrated with foodId=null but the reverse-lookup does not re-fire. The changed-check inside setRows is correct but never executes with prev containing rows to enrich. LIVE PROOF: rowsMissingFoodId=92, rowsWithFoodId=0, totalMatchCount=92 (would-match count if executed).

RecipeBulkEditor.jsx L208 (BUG-206 validation): The new client-side fail-fast check correctly prevents the confusing server 422 and surfaces a clearer error. Good defensive coding. However, it now blocks all existing standard recipe saves until the L97-111 enrichment actually runs. This is the right place for the guard, but the underlying enrichment must actually work.

RecipeFormPanel.jsx L50-56 (working reference): The BUG-197 #7 workaround does the reverse-lookup INSIDE the async loader (single useEffect), matching against `recipe.foodName` (not `recipe.name`). RecipeBulkEditor matches against `row.name` which is populated from `r.name || r.food_name` in fromAPI.recipes L11 — so for existing recipes, row.name IS the food_name (confirmed: '50-50 Choco Lava'). Match logic is correct — only the effect ordering is broken.

Consider extracting foodsMaster loading into a shared hook (useFoodsMaster) since both RecipeFormPanel and RecipeBulkEditor need it. Currently uses different services (getActiveFoods vs getFoodsList) which return slightly different food records — a maintenance risk.
